title: KV strategy constructor: hit-sensitivity matrix, TTL laddering, and safe apply playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem statement: We need an automated, conservative approach to recommend KV/prefix caching configs (key design, TTL bands, hit-rate expectations) and to apply them with clear safety gates. Current manual tuning is slow, inconsistent between tenants, and leads to transient regressions in tail latency and quality. This ticket defines a reproducible 'strategy constructor' that synthesizes recommendations from production telemetry + synthetic workloads, produces a hit-sensitivity matrix for candidate policies, and automates a staged apply/rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline that ingests prefix-level telemetry and outputs candidate cache policies (keying, TTL bands, prefetch hints)
Hit-sensitivity matrix generated for each candidate policy with expected cost delta and hit-rate risk estimate
A canary/staged apply process (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%) implemented with automatic safety gates and a documented rollback path
Runbook and dashboard tiles added to Console for realtime monitoring during rollouts
Load tests and synthetic validation using 'kvforge' generator demonstrate no more than 2% p95 latency regression under expected traffic for accepted policies
implementation_steps: Build 'kvforge' synthetic workload generator that replays prefix distributions with adjustable skew and cold-start ratios
Implement hit-sensitivity matrix exporter: given baseline telemetry and candidate TTLs/key-shaping produce expected hit-rate, cost delta, and tail latency model
Create policy composer that suggests TTL ladders (e.g., [15s, 1m, 5m, 1h]) and prefix-normalization rules for canonical keys
Add safety gates: min_net_savings >= 5%, hit_rate_drop_limit <= 2 percentage points, error_rate_delta < 0.5%
Implement staged rollout orchestration in console: shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers
Instrument dashboards and alerts: kvcache.hitrate.{p50,p90,p99}, kvcache.backend.calls, runtime.batch_wait_ms
Run controlled experiments on internal cluster and validate with benchmark suite, then schedule customer canary
notes: Key hygiene rules: normalize unicode, strip ephemeral client-side tokens, apply deterministic shard prefix where appropriate
Prefer prefix coalescing for high-cardinality tails to avoid over-sampling low-value keys
Batching interactions: ensure recommended TTLs don't dramatically increase hot-partition batch sizes that raise token emission latency
We should prefer conservative initial TTL bands and use autotune to expand lifetimes if safety gate metrics hold
Operational constraints: for Dedicated tenants, we must respect isolation constraints and offer recommendations as opt-in policies
decisions: Use a hybrid estimator combining production sampling + kvforge counterfactual replay rather than pure modeling to reduce mismatch
Safety gates are intentionally strict (5% savings threshold) to avoid noisy rollouts; we can relax after N successful rollouts
Rollout windows: 48h shadow observation, 24h at 1% and 72h at 10% before promoting to 100%, unless safety alerts fire earlier
Policy output format: JSON policy with key_rules, ttl_bands, prefetch_hints, and rollout_profile – designed to be human-readable in Console and machine-applyable via API
